title: [8/9/2023] Proportion of UK residents interested in sports
prompt: The chart shows the proportion of people in a UK survey carried out in three different years who said they were interested in certain sports. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make a comparison where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the percentages of UK residents who expressed interest in six different sports, based on surveys conducted in 1995, 2000, and 2005.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while interest in football, swimming and rugby showed an upward trend over the period, the figures for snooker and tennis declined slightly, and golf's popularity remained relatively stable. Throughout the given timeframe, football consistently maintained its position as the most popular sport among UK residents.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the sports that showed an overall increase, in 1995, football led with 41% of respondents showing interest, while swimming attracted 22% and rugby 24%. Football maintained its dominant position with a steady rise, reaching 44% by 2005. Swimming saw more substantial changes, increasing to 29% in 2000 before slightly declining to 27% in the final year, while rugby showed notable fluctuation, dropping to 19% in 2000 before recovering strongly to 27% by 2005.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining sports, both snooker and tennis recorded relatively high interest levels in 1995, at 30% and 29% respectively, while golf attracted only 17% of respondents. Snooker experienced the most dramatic decline, falling sharply to 21% in 2000 before recovering slightly to 23% by 2005. Tennis showed a similar but more moderate decrease, dropping to 22% in 2000 and maintaining this level until the end of the period, while golf's popularity remained relatively stable, fluctuating only slightly between 15% and 17% throughout the decade.
